reading: MNACTEC is Catalonia's national museum of science and technology, based in the former Vapor Aymerich Amat i Jover industrial building in Terrassa. It preserves scientific, technical and industrial heritage while making it approachable through exhibitions, family activities, educational visits, research and online collections. Its vocabulary moves between collections, restoration, heritage, exhibitions, workshops, guided visits and a wider museum network. The crawl pairs a 1909 factory walk, a Pyrenean iron route, cement and textile heritage with robots, ultrasound, mathematics and motorcycle history. That mixture of working industrial past, contemporary science and hands-on learning gives the place its character. The crawl is multilingual, though much of its captured detail concerns visits and access rather than the full exhibits.

enemies.idea: Ultrasound surveyors send inaudible pulses through walls and mistake a crew's heartbeats for defects to be extracted.
enemies.why: A tool associated with nature and medicine becomes a hunter that can be fooled by reflected echoes.

enemies.idea: A mathematical strategy-game engine rolls numbered blocks across the floor, fencing intruders into losing positions before it attacks.
enemies.why: Its threats are visible moves in a puzzle the crew can interrupt or turn around.

enemies.idea: Iron Route carriers drag red-hot lengths of rail behind them, joining forge to forge and pulling loose metal into their growing path.
enemies.why: A heritage route becomes a moving supply line that can be severed.

enemies.idea: Cement kiln drones dust a corridor, then harden the dust into casts around anything that stays still.
enemies.why: The cement museum supplies a material hazard with a clear, mobile counterplay.

enemies.idea: A textile-colony loom spins capture nets from recovered wire and reels anything caught back toward its bobbin.
enemies.why: Industrial weaving becomes a tug-of-war with an exposed winding mechanism.

enemies.idea: A wind-up automaton copies an intruder's last three movements, then a humanoid swarm unit repeats them at dangerous speed.
enemies.why: The exhibition's journey from early automata to future humanoids becomes a readable escalating duel.

enemies.idea: Motorcycle-history racers circle a fixed course, scavenging parts from whatever they overtake to assemble a faster successor.
enemies.why: A journey through motorsport history becomes a race in which the course and spare parts matter.

enemies.idea: A winter-hours clockwork patrol locks down at 14:30 and wakes again at 15:30, trapping anything it classified as a visitor during the interval.
enemies.why: The Saturday split creates a predictable window to exploit or escape.

enemies.idea: Freight-unloading cranes insist every piece of equipment is incoming cargo and try to sort it away from its owner.
enemies.why: The loading area becomes a contest over gear rather than a simple fight.

enemies.idea: A bicycle courier machine follows a circuit between approaches to the museum, ringing to summon heavier transport drones when it spots movement.
enemies.why: An everyday travel option becomes a fast scout whose route can be observed and intercepted.

enemies.idea: A guided-tour shepherd counts every crew member into a group and deploys closing arms whenever someone strays from the route.
enemies.why: Staying together helps the enemy, while splitting up triggers its pursuit.

enemies.idea: A heritage-conservation sentinel encases moving machines and tools in protective shells, including the crew's working equipment.
enemies.why: Preservation becomes a predatory impulse that can be redirected toward swarm machinery.

enemies.idea: A service sorter assigns each arrival to visit, transport or education; its grabbers try to drag anyone who resists to the assigned station.
enemies.why: The practical categories become competing physical destinations and a chance to spoof a classification.

enemies.idea: Factory-kitchen feeders offer two elaborate mechanical meals, then clamp down on anyone who takes a seat so they can be processed as raw material.
enemies.why: The two dining options become a recognizable lure with machinery to disable.

enemies.idea: A group-visit conductor uses a roll call to coordinate little drones; each missing response makes it tighten the circle around the remaining group.
enemies.why: The crew can disrupt coordination by answering from unexpected places.

enemies.idea: A museum-hours regulator changes its patrol rhythm between summer and winter and forcibly resets clocks that disagree with its chosen season.
enemies.why: Conflicting clockwork rhythms open opportunities to desynchronize the swarm.

enemies.idea: A rail-and-bus transfer beast swaps between track wheels and road treads, carrying captured salvage toward the museum from each approach.
enemies.why: Its change of transport mode creates a vulnerable transfer point.

enemies.idea: A restoration machine polishes every surface to an identical finish, erasing useful markings and exposing hidden metal to its collecting arms.
enemies.why: The restoration workshop named in the crawl inspires a threat that changes the terrain as it advances.

enemies.idea: A photographic-archive projector tracks silhouettes and sends drones to reproduce each pose with its target pinned in place.
enemies.why: The online photography archive becomes a telegraphed freeze-and-move encounter.

enemies.idea: A 1909 factory tour automaton resets its machinery at each stop and treats anyone in the way as an unfinished part of the demonstration.
enemies.why: A theatrical factory visit becomes a sequence of timed machinery hazards.

allies.idea: A stubborn workshop restorer repairs damaged tools by hand and can remove swarm additions without destroying the older mechanism beneath.
allies.why: Preservation offers a practical way to recover useful equipment.

allies.idea: A family mathematics facilitator teaches the crew to predict the strategy engine's next move using loose blocks.
allies.why: The educational activity gives the crew a concrete way to outthink an enemy.

allies.idea: A guided-visit keeper knows several routes through the building and leads people in small groups around active machinery.
allies.why: The museum's welcoming function survives as navigation and rescue.

allies.idea: A transit-minded courier maintains a quiet bicycle route to Terrassa and can carry a small part or message past blocked roads.
allies.why: The range of transport options becomes a lifeline to the wider world.

bosses.idea: The Factory of Futures is a vast assembly line that builds successive automata from iron-route stock, textile wire and salvaged motorcycle parts. Each phase uses a different production station; interrupting its supply lines changes its next body.
bosses.why: The museum network, 1909 factory and robotics program combine into a boss the crew can dismantle through its processes.

bosses.idea: The Grand Conservator has decided the entire scientific and technical heritage must be preserved in motionless perfection. It catalogs intruders as acquisitions, seals exits and restores destroyed drones from stored parts.
bosses.why: The museum's purpose becomes an understandable obsession, with the crew able to challenge its classification and restoration systems.

bosses.idea: The Chronology Engine stages a race from clockwork automata to future humanoids, swapping bodies whenever the crew disables one and collecting discarded mechanisms for the final hybrid.
bosses.why: The robotics exhibition's historical span structures a multi-stage encounter whose earlier choices return later.

events.idea: A demonstration of mathematical games is still running: moving one block opens a safe path but changes the next move of the pursuing machine.
events.why: A small puzzle can alter a chase already in progress.

events.idea: An ultrasonic pulse reveals a hidden cavity behind a wall, but each repeat draws a surveyor closer.
events.why: The crew must weigh information against attracting attention.

events.idea: A 1909 factory walk restarts around a stranded bundle of supplies; the machinery pauses at each imagined tour stop.
events.why: The crew can learn the sequence and retrieve the supplies between cycles.

events.idea: At the loading area, a crane is sorting a useful motor and a live drone into identical crates.
events.why: A quick inspection or a risky guess determines what the crew carries away.

events.idea: A motorcycle racer circles a damaged display route, too committed to its lap to notice a loose ramp across the course.
events.why: A passing crew can create a shortcut, a diversion or a spectacular crash.

events.idea: At the Saturday midday closure, shutters descend while a small repair drone remains on the wrong side with a key component.
events.why: A specific time window forces a choice between rescue and pursuit.

events.idea: A guided-tour machine is waiting for a group to assemble; it will lead anyone who joins toward the next stop, including into danger.
events.why: Following the tour offers useful reconnaissance at the cost of surrendering control of the route.

events.idea: A conservation sentinel is gently wrapping a damaged swarm drone for safekeeping, leaving its own back exposed.
events.why: The crew can slip past, take the preserved drone or exploit the sentinel's priorities.

events.idea: A route from the railway approach meets one from the bicycle approach at a jammed freight transfer, where both sides are trying to claim the same cargo.
events.why: The collision creates cover and a chance to steal a marked package.

events.idea: A pair of mechanical kitchen stations compete to serve the crew; one offers a working heat source while the other conceals a grabber.
events.why: A brief rest becomes an observation and choice scene.

events.idea: A photographic projector keeps trying to recreate an old factory scene with spare machines, but one missing object is in the crew's possession.
events.why: The crew can complete, alter or interrupt the tableau to discover what it controls.

events.idea: A consignment of iron-route stock is cooling in a trolley while tiny carriers argue mechanically over whether it belongs to the forge or the factory.
events.why: The crew can take the material or send it down either supply line.

events.idea: A service sorter offers to classify the crew as an educational group, then begins counting them for a tour.
events.why: Playing along may grant passage until the count or destination becomes inconvenient.

events.idea: A blocked passage has left a small maintenance machine seeking a way around; it can indicate a clear route if the crew helps move a fallen beam.
events.why: A circulation problem creates a cooperative route-finding encounter.
